Input data for the trade package: trade_RAW

Source: vignettes/input-trade-data.Rmd
input-trade-data.Rmd

OECD project on SME scaling up. For information: scaleup@oecd.org, juergen.amann@oecd.org.

The trade package (run_trade_pipeline()) adds firm-level international trade in goods to the scale-up indicators. It reads the same base_financials_<CT>.dta (and, if present, plants_RAW_<CT>.dta, tl3_typology.dta, exchange_rates.dta) as the scale-up pipeline, described in vignette("input-data"), plus one trade file. The same information is in the package dataset variable_dictionary (?variable_dictionary). check_inputs(cfg) also checks trade_RAW_<CT>.dta when it is in input_dir.

File

trade_RAW_<CT>.dta in config$input_dir, where <CT> is the two-letter country code given to config_scaleup(). It holds transaction-level international trade in goods statistics (ITGS): one row per firm, year, flow (import or export), destination country and 8-digit CN product.

General rules

  1. Missing values are coded . in numeric variables and "." in string variables. The package also reads an empty string as missing.
  2. trade_value is in EUR thousand. Values in euros are declared with config_scaleup(trade_value_unit = "EUR"), and the build divides them by
    1. (For PT and HU, which delivered euros in earlier rounds, "EUR" is the default.)
  3. Definitions follow the Eurostat (2022) European business statistics compilers’ manual for international trade in goods statistics, detailed data: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-manuals-and-guidelines/-/ks-gq-22-008.

Priorities

All the variables of trade_RAW are must-have: the trade build stops if one is missing.

What to supply

Variable Priority Definition Format and coding Source Notes
idf must-have unique firm-level identifier numeric Allows the data to be joined with base_financials.
year must-have calendar year numeric
trade_type must-have indicator of import or export numeric; 1 = import; 2 = export
trade_value must-have statistical value, in EUR thousand numeric ITGS See 8.7.1.2 of the ITGS compilers’ manual.
code_destin must-have the last country to which it is known, at the time of export, that the goods are to be exported string; two-letter country code, e.g. SE for Sweden ITGS See 8.5.3.1 and 8.5.2.1 of the ITGS compilers’ manual. Non-missing for trade_type == 2.
prod_code must-have goods code at CN level (8 digits) string ITGS See 8.4.1 of the ITGS compilers’ manual.

What the package does with it

Variable The package needs it What the package does with it
idf required Links the trade records to base_financials. Firm-years of base_financials without trade records are non-traders (value 0); trade records of firms not in base_financials are dropped.
year required Trade is summed per firm and year.
trade_type required Splits the flows into imports (imp_) and exports (exp_). A missing trade_type stops the build. A file with only one flow gives missing values for the other.
trade_value required Summed to exp_value / imp_value per firm-year (exporter, importer, heavy and light exporting scalers HGX / HGNX). Products whose 6-digit total is below 1 (EUR thousand) are left out. Declare config_scaleup(trade_value_unit = “EUR”) for values in euros.
code_destin required Number of export destinations (exp_all_partners) and of EU destinations (exp_eu_partners, EU membership of the year).
prod_code required Cut to its first 6 characters (HS6): number of products (exp_products, imp_products) and the share of the largest product (exp_core_prod, imp_core_prod).

The trade build (build_trade_panel() and build_trade_accounts_indicators()) collapses the transactions to one row per firm and year and merges them onto base_financials:

  • exp_value, imp_value: total exports and imports (EUR thousand); exporter, importer: 1 for a positive value;
  • exp_all_partners, exp_eu_partners: number of export destinations, all and in the EU;
  • exp_products, imp_products: number of 6-digit products; exp_core_prod, imp_core_prod: share of the largest product;
  • y4_exporter: first-time exporters over t-3 to t;
  • HGX10, HGX20, HGNX10, HGNX20: turnover scalers whose export growth is at least (heavy exporting) or less than (light exporting) half the turnover growth that makes a high-growth firm;
  • sector_exporter, digit_sect: sector group by export status, and by the digital intensity of the industry.

Import partner countries are not part of the data, so there are no import partner counts.
